title: Shared Plotly-native themes and styles
objective: Define deterministic notebook, presentation, publication, dark, and high-contrast plotting themes with colorblind-conscious palettes, normalized line/marker/text/fill style contracts, and JSON-safe Plotly defaults shared by 2D, 3D, and all frontends.

oracles: Theme registry fixtures, contrast checks, and CPython/Sage.js differential Plotly defaults

handoff.summary: Added five deterministic, immutable/copy-safe Plotly-native themes (notebook, presentation, publication, dark, and high-contrast), strict supported/translated/unsupported line/marker/fill/text option normalization, the full Plotly CSS named-color table, WCAG-like contrast metrics, synchronized checked documentation, and focused tests with byte-exact CPython/Sage.js differential output plus installed Plotly 3.7 schema and Chromium rendering checks for 2D scatter, surface, and mesh traces.
risks: The broad integration receipt fails in this lane because optional native FLINT headers, generated FFI manifests, compiled kernels, and packages/flint/build/Release/sagejs_flint.node are not provisioned; 172 of 413 tests pass and the failures are unrelated to this pure-Python plotting slice.

The real Plotly rendering portion of the focused test skips on hosts without Chrome or Chromium, while deterministic differential, documentation, style-outcome, copy-safety, and contrast checks continue to run.

Themes configure hover labels and responsive Plotly interactions but cannot by themselves guarantee keyboard navigation, focus order, or screen-reader semantics; the checked documentation states this boundary explicitly.
next_steps: The integration lane should export selected theme/style APIs from sagejs.plotting, add themes.py and styles.py to the central Pyright strict-module list, and add test/plot-themes.cjs to the central test manifest.
Unified lowering should merge theme layout/config/trace defaults before user PlotSpec overrides so explicit plot options remain authoritative.
Downstream semantic layer planners can retain OptionResult.to_dict() decisions in provenance and fail only when a decision has status unsupported.
